events.text: {npc} runs the ferry across the narrow sea of {pw_world}, as {his} mother did and {his} mother's mother. The family has a story about you: that their first boat was built from a tree you showed them. They would like to know if it is true.
events.arc: The Ferry Across the First Sea

choices.text: Tell {npc} which tree, and where its stump is

effects.log: You walk {him} up the headland to a stump gone soft as cake. {npc} kneels and touches it, and takes a piece of it home for the new boat.

choices.text: Say you do not remember

effects.log: {npc} looks relieved and disappointed at once. "Then we built it ourselves," {he} says, and straightens.

choices.text: Ride the ferry across and back, saying nothing

effects.log: You ride it all day. The boat is well built. By sunset {npc} has decided you are either a fool or a spirit, and gives you the evening crossing free.

events.text: A storm wrecks the ferry family's boat. {npc} has a new hull half-built and no time: the harvest of the far shore has to come across before the cold, or it rots and {pw_kingdom} goes hungry.
events.arc: The Ferry Across the First Sea

choices.text: Work on the hull with {npc} day and night

effects.log: Nine days. You plane and caulk and argue about the keel. The boat goes in the water on the tenth, and the harvest comes home.

choices.text: Carry the grain across yourself, a cart at a time

ok.log: For a week the fishermen watch a figure walk the shallows with sacks, back and forth, in the cold. They tell their children about it forever.

fail.log: The sea is colder than you are strong. You get half the harvest across and spend a season coughing.

choices.text: Let the far shore keep its harvest this year

effects.log: The far shore eats well. The near shore eats less. {npc} never says a word about it, and that is worse.

events.text: {npc}'s grandchild takes the ferry now. {npc} sits on the jetty and mends nets, and asks you to take a last crossing with {him} in the old boat, before it is broken up.
events.arc: The Ferry Across the First Sea

choices.text: Row, and let {npc} steer

effects.log: You row. {npc} steers by memory, eyes half-closed. Halfway across {he} says "here" and you both stop and let the boat drift, and listen to the water.

choices.text: Tell {npc} the story of the first boat, the true one

effects.log: {npc} listens to the end. "Better than ours," {he} says, "but we will keep ours."

choices.text: Carve the family's name on the bow before it is broken

effects.log: They keep the bow-board and hang it in the house. You carved it a little crooked. Nobody minds.

events.text: {npc}, the young queen of {pw_kingdom}, comes to your door with two guards and no ceremony. {He} has been told that you are the oldest person in {pw_world} and wants to ask how {his} kingdom looked when it was small.
events.arc: The Queen Who Asked the Oldest Living

choices.text: Tell {him} honestly: muddy, loud and happy

effects.log: {He} laughs, and then listens closely, and asks about the mud. When {he} leaves {he} has a plan for the drains.

choices.text: Show {him} the old border stones in your fields

effects.log: They are knee-high and sunk in grass. {He} sits on one and looks at {his} kingdom from outside it for the first time.

choices.text: Say kingdoms look better from far off

effects.log: {He} frowns, then nods. {He} does not come back for ten years, and when {he} does, {he} is wiser and less polite.

events.text: {npc} is at war with a neighbour over a river valley, and losing. {He} comes back, older, and asks the question {he} should not: will you fight for {pw_kingdom}?
events.arc: The Queen Who Asked the Oldest Living

choices.text: Refuse, and tell {him} why

effects.log: "If I fight for one crown I belong to it." {He} does not like it. {He} respects it. {He} makes peace instead, at a price, and reigns another forty years.

choices.text: Stand at the ford for one day only

ok.log: The other army sees who is standing at the ford, and decides the valley was never worth it. The war ends without a battle.

fail.log: They come anyway. You hold the ford until dark and are carried home on a door. The war ends a month later in a draw.

choices.text: Go and talk to the other ruler

effects.log: The other ruler is a frightened young man who also came to ask you a question once. You make them have dinner together. The valley is shared.

events.text: {npc} is old, and has written down everything you told {him} about the small kingdom for {his} heirs. {He} sends the book to you with a note asking what {he} got wrong.
events.arc: The Queen Who Asked the Oldest Living

choices.text: Correct it gently, in the margins

effects.log: Your notes are longer than {his} book. The heirs of {pw_kingdom} read them both, the book for the history and the margins for the jokes.

choices.text: Send it back with no changes

effects.log: "Your memory is the kingdom's now," you write. {He} keeps the note in the front of the book.

choices.text: Bring it back to {him} in person

effects.log: You read it to {him} aloud, by a window. {He} corrects you twice. It is a good afternoon, and {he} is smiling at the end of it.

events.text: {npc} is drawing the first map of the whole of {pw_world}. {He} has walked for twenty years and filled most of it, but there are blanks, and the old people say you have walked where nobody else has.
events.arc: The Map of the Whole World

choices.text: Draw the blanks for {him} from memory

effects.log: You fill in a mountain range, a salt lake and a forest older than the kingdoms. {npc} checks the forest. It is exactly where you said.

choices.text: Walk the blanks with {npc}

effects.log: Three years on the road. {npc} is good company and terrible at cooking. The map gets its blanks and a great many notes about soup.

choices.text: Leave some places blank on purpose

effects.log: You tell {him} about all of it but one valley. Some places should stay unmapped. {npc} draws it in as "here are wonders" and is not wrong.

events.text: The map is copied and sold all over {pw_world}. A rich trader wants {npc} to mark the old places of power on the next edition, the springs and caves where the energy pools. {npc} asks you.
events.arc: The Map of the Whole World

choices.text: Tell {him} to leave them off

effects.log: {npc} leaves them off and loses the trader's money. The springs stay clean. Pilgrims still find them, the slow way.

choices.text: Mark only the ones that can take the crowds

effects.log: You choose three that will not be ruined by visitors. They become famous. The others stay quiet.

choices.text: Mark them all: the world is everyone's

effects.log: The springs fill with seekers. Some are ruined, and some make masters out of farmers. {npc} is rich, and not sure how to feel.

events.text: {npc} is the last who speaks the old tongue of {pw_people} as a mother tongue. {He} is very old and very cross that nobody listens, and has heard that you might.
events.arc: The Old Tongue of the First People

choices.text: Learn it from {him}

effects.log: It takes four years. The old tongue has eleven words for the light before dawn and none for owning land. You understand {pw_people} better than you did.

choices.text: Write it down as {he} speaks

effects.log: You fill a chest with paper. {npc} reads none of it and corrects all of it.

choices.text: Find the children who will learn it

effects.log: Three children, one of them very reluctant. {npc} is a terrible teacher and they love {him}.

events.text: The old tongue is coming back, a little: songs at weddings, names for children. {npc} wants one more thing before {he} is done: the old prayer to the maker of the world spoken aloud at the high stone, once, by someone who understands it.
events.arc: The Old Tongue of the First People

choices.text: Speak it yourself at the high stone

effects.log: You speak it. Something in the sky over {pw_world} listens, the way a parent listens from the next room. {npc} hears it too, and weeps.

choices.text: Let the reluctant child speak it

effects.log: The child stumbles twice and finishes. The whole village holds its breath and lets it go. {npc} is prouder than if {he} had said it alone.

choices.text: Let it be spoken by everyone, badly

effects.log: Two hundred voices, all wrong in different places. It is the most beautiful thing you have heard in a century.

events.text: {npc} has founded a lodge of fighters in a market town and wants an old master to sit on its bench, so that the young ones will believe the arts are older than {npc}. {He} offers a room, rice and a great deal of respect.

choices.text: Accept, for a while

effects.log: You sit on the bench. The young ones are frightened of you for a month and then not, which is better. The lodge grows.

choices.text: Teach one lesson a year, no more

effects.log: Your one lesson a year becomes the lodge's great day. Fighters walk from across {pw_kingdom} to hear it.

choices.text: Decline: a lodge should grow its own elders

effects.log: {npc} is hurt, then thoughtful. In thirty years the lodge has elders of its own, and they are good.

events.text: A rival lodge has challenged {npc}'s lodge to a contest of champions, and {npc}'s best student has broken an arm. The rival lodge has made it very clear that an old bench-sitter cannot stand in.

choices.text: Train the second-best student for a month

effects.log: The student is fast and frightened. You make that speed slower and braver. The student wins by a hair, and nobody at {npc}'s lodge ever lets the matter drop.

choices.text: Stand in anyway, and dare them to object

ok.log: They object loudly, and then their champion steps in and very quickly steps out again. The rival lodge sends a gift by morning.

fail.log: Their champion is good, and young, and lucky. You lose a hard bout with grace, and both lodges toast you with tea.

choices.text: Make both lodges cancel and hold a feast

effects.log: {npc} is furious and then relieved. The two lodges eat together and find they hate the same tax collector.

events.text: {npc} has come from the far side of {pw_world} to ask you one thing: what the world was like before {pw_kingdom}, when there were only {pw_people} and the empty land.
variants: A child of {pw_people}, {npc}, has been sent by {his} village with a basket of eggs and a list of questions in a careful hand. The first question is how old you are.
{npc}, a singer, has come to learn the oldest songs of {pw_world}. {He} sings you the ones {he} knows, to see which you remember differently.

choices.text: Tell {npc} about the empty land

effects.log: You tell {him} about the first fires, and the long quiet. {npc} goes home and tells it to {his} grandchildren, who tell it wrong, beautifully.

choices.text: Take {npc} to see a place that has not changed

effects.log: There is one valley that looks the way it did. You take {him} there, and {he} sits down in the grass and does not speak.

choices.text: Say you do not remember, so the past stays theirs

effects.log: {npc} is disappointed, and then not. "Then we can make it up," {he} says, and goes home happy.

events.text: {npc}, the best young fighter in {pw_kingdom}, has come to test the oldest master in {pw_world}, because nobody else is left to test.
variants: {npc} has walked a month to find you, and stands in your yard with a staff and a great deal of hope. {He} has been told you are the strongest thing in {pw_world} that is not a god.

choices.text: Accept the test

ok.log: You give {him} a long fight and a clear lesson. {npc} bows to the ground and asks to come back in ten years.

fail.log: {npc} is stronger than you thought the world could make anyone yet. You lose a hard exchange, and are glad.

choices.text: Set {npc} a task instead

effects.log: "Climb the high stone and tell me what you see." {npc} goes, offended, and comes back three days later having seen something. You talk until dawn.

choices.text: Send {npc} home to {his} teacher

effects.log: "Beat your teacher first." {npc} goes home and does, and the teacher writes you a very rude letter.

events.text: The first frost of the year in {pw_world}, on the same morning as always. You have seen it so many times that you notice what is different: the frost is thinner, the world a little warmer than when it was young.
variants: The long rains of {pw_world}. You remember when the world had no rains at all, only the first dew, and the first people lay on their backs to drink it from the air.
Spring in {pw_world}, and the birds that came back are the great-great-grandchildren of birds you fed. They do not know you. They sit on your fence anyway.
Summer in {pw_world}, and the heat sits on the land like a hand. You remember summers when the world was young and had no idea how hot it could get.
The geese of {pw_world} are going south over your roof in a line that stretches from one horizon to the other. They have done it every year since there were geese.

choices.text: Sit out in it until noon

effects.log: The frost melts around you in a ring. Something of the world's slow breath comes into yours.

choices.text: Walk to the old frost-line and mark the change

effects.log: You set a stone where the frost reaches now. It is a good way from the stone you set last time.

choices.text: Bring in the late gourds before they spoil

effects.log: Practical work in cold air. Your hands are red and your mind is very clear.

events.text: A beast has come down from the high places of {pw_world}, older and larger than anything the villages have seen, and it is standing in the barley. {npc}, the headwoman, asks the old master to do something.
variants: Something huge is in the river shallows of the kingdom, blocking the ferry. {npc}, who runs the ferry, has come to ask the old master whether it can be argued with.
The beasts of the high places are restless this year, and one of them has come down to the river meadows of the kingdom. {npc} asks the old master to come and see it.
Something old has come down from the mountains of {pw_world} and is sleeping in the middle of the high road. {npc}, whose village is on the other side, has come for help.

choices.text: Face the beast

ok.log: It is old and proud. You meet it in the barley, and it decides, after a long look, to go home. The barley is flat for an acre.

fail.log: It is stronger than you. You turn it back up the slope at the cost of a torn shoulder, and the village bandages you with great ceremony.

choices.text: Find out why it came down

effects.log: A fire on the high slopes, a dry spring. You go up and clear the spring. The beast follows you back up, curious, and stays there.

choices.text: Tell the village to give it the field

effects.log: It eats an acre of barley and lies down in the sun and is still there a hundred years later, a hill with a heartbeat. The children climb it.

events.text: The day of the dead in {pw_world}. Your list of graves is longer than any family's in {pw_kingdom}, and some of the stones are older than the kingdom.
variants: You find a grave of the people you did not know you would find: a friend from the first centuries, under a road. The carts go over it every day. It is, you think, the kind of grave they would have liked.

choices.text: Visit every one

effects.log: A month of walking. At the oldest stone, whose words are gone, you say the name aloud for whoever is listening.

choices.text: Tell the young the names

effects.log: You sit in the market and tell anyone who stops whose the old stones were. Some of them come back next year to hear more.

choices.text: Plant a tree for the ones without stones

effects.log: There are a great many. You plant one tree for all of them, in the middle of {pw_kingdom}, where everyone passes.

events.text: A gang has been robbing the long road through {pw_kingdom}, and tonight they stop the oldest traveller in the world. {npc}, the one in charge, has a speech prepared.
variants: Three robbers in masks made from flour sacks step out of the trees. {npc}, the smallest, has a voice that has not broken yet.
On the long road through {pw_kingdom}, a fallen tree, and behind it a gang with clubs. {npc}, at the front, has clearly never done this before.
{npc} and a dozen others have been taking a toll at the old bridge, at knifepoint. Tonight the oldest traveller in the world wants to cross.

choices.text: Let {npc} finish the speech, then answer it

ok.log: It is a short answer. The gang wakes up in a heap by the road, tied with their own belts.

fail.log: There are more of them than the speech implied. You get home with a black eye and most of your bag.

choices.text: Ask {npc} why {he} took to the road

effects.log: A burned farm, a debt, a winter. You give {him} work on your land. {npc} is a bad farmer and a loyal one.

choices.text: Hand over the bag: it is mostly turnips

effects.log: {npc} is very disappointed in the turnips. You walk on, lighter.

events.text: {pw_kingdom} holds its great harvest feast. The people have a custom now: the oldest living person sets the first lantern on the water. They come for you with a lantern and a great deal of noise.
variants: The midwinter fires of the world. The young of the people jump the flames for luck, and they have decided this year that the oldest living must jump first.
The spring feast of {pw_kingdom}: blossom on every roof, and a procession that will not start until the oldest living has walked at its head.
The feast of the first harvest of the world, older than {pw_kingdom}. The children have made a crown of wheat, and they are looking for the oldest head to put it on.
The night of lamps in {pw_kingdom}. Every window has a light in it, and the people have decided yours should be lit first.

choices.text: Set the lantern on the water

effects.log: It floats out, and a thousand more follow it. You stand on the bank until the last one goes round the bend, and feel the world loved.

choices.text: Give the lantern to the youngest child there

effects.log: The child sets it down so carefully that it tips over. Everyone cheers anyway. The custom changes that night, for good.

choices.text: Make a lantern for each of the dead you remember

effects.log: It takes all day. When you set them on the water the people go quiet, and set theirs after, one at a time.

events.text: Three young people of {pw_people} are sitting outside your door, as they have been for nine days. They want to be taught, and have decided that sitting is how one asks.
variants: A girl of {pw_people} has been throwing stones at your roof every morning for a month. When you finally come out she asks, very loudly, to be your student.
A boy of {pw_people} has followed you home from the market, at a respectful distance, for the third day running. Today he has brought a staff.
Two sisters of {pw_people} have walked from the far side of the kingdom with a letter from their village, which says only: teach them.

choices.text: Teach them

effects.log: You teach them for ten years. They are very different and all good, and when they go they take your arts into three corners of {pw_world}.

choices.text: Teach the one who left first

effects.log: On the tenth morning one gave up and went home to the farm. You follow, and teach that one in the evenings, between the ploughing.

choices.text: Send them to the lodges in {pw_kingdom}

effects.log: They go, disappointed, and do well. The lodges hear where they came from and treat them with suspicious respect.

events.text: The rains have failed in {pw_kingdom} for the second year. The fields are cracked, the river is a string of pools, and the people of the villages are walking to your door to ask the oldest living what was done before.

choices.text: Show them the old water roads under the hills

effects.log: You remember where the water ran before the kingdom. They dig where you point, and find it, cold and sweet.

choices.text: Pray at the high stone to the maker of the world

effects.log: You climb the high stone and speak plainly. Three days later it rains. Whether it was the prayer, nobody can say.

choices.text: Teach them to save the water they have

effects.log: Cisterns, terraces, covered channels. It is hard work and slow, and the next drought does not touch them.

events.text: A child of {pw_people} has wandered off into the hills and the village is out with lanterns. You can hear the child, very small and far off, singing to keep brave.

choices.text: Follow the song and bring the child down

effects.log: The child is sitting on a rock, still singing, and stops in the middle of a line to ask who you are. You carry the child home on your shoulders.

choices.text: Light a fire where the searchers will see it

effects.log: They see it, and find the child beside it, warm. The village argues for a week about who lit it.

variants: Fog in the hills of the kingdom, and somewhere in it a child calling for a dog. The dog is home. The child is not.
A child of {pw_people} has gone into the old forest after a fox, and the fox has come out alone.

events.text: {npc} is the only other person in {pw_world} nearly as old as you. Every fifty years the two of you meet on the same bridge and argue about what really happened in the first century of {pw_kingdom}.

choices.text: Argue, as always

effects.log: You argue all day. Neither of you is right. You part the best of friends, as always.

choices.text: Concede a point, for once

effects.log: {npc} is so astonished that {he} concedes one back. It is the most interesting conversation the bridge has heard in a thousand years.

choices.text: Bring the young to listen

effects.log: A crowd gathers. By evening the two oldest people in {pw_world} are a festival, and somebody is selling buns.

events.text: You dream of the one who made {pw_world}: not a face, only a sense of being looked at, kindly, from very far away, the way a gardener looks at a bed of seedlings.
variants: You dream that {pw_world} is very small and held in two hands, and that the hands are tired, and careful. You wake up wanting to be careful too.
You dream that you are walking through {pw_world} beside someone very tall, who is looking at everything as if seeing how it turned out.
In the dream there is a workbench, and on it {pw_world}, half-finished, and the tools laid down very carefully, as if someone meant to come back.

choices.text: Look back

effects.log: In the dream you look back, and for a moment the gardener is surprised. You wake with a feeling that you have been recognised.

choices.text: Ask the dream a question

effects.log: You ask why the world was made. The dream does not answer, but the feeling of being looked at grows warmer, which may be the answer.

choices.text: Let it be only a dream

effects.log: You wake and go about your day, and the day is very good, for no reason.

events.text: Raiders from the wild borderlands of {pw_world} have come down on a village of {pw_people} at harvest. {npc}, their chief, has heard the village has an old protector and has come to see for themselves.

choices.text: Show {npc}

ok.log: You show {him}. The raiders go home without the harvest, and the borderlands sing about it, not kindly.

fail.log: {npc} is as strong as the songs say. You drive the raiders off at a cost, and the village nurses you through the winter.

choices.text: Offer {npc} a share of the harvest, freely given

effects.log: {npc} takes it, puzzled. The next year the borderlands trade with the village instead of raiding it.

choices.text: Hide the village in the hills until they pass

effects.log: The raiders find empty houses and a burned field. The village lives, and rebuilds, and is angry with you for a decade.

events.text: A storm on the first sea of {pw_world}, the worst in a century, and three fishing boats are still out. The harbour of {pw_kingdom} is full of people shouting at the waves.

choices.text: Go out to them

ok.log: You walk out on the breakwater and further, and bring the boats in one by one through the rocks. Nobody in the harbour ever forgets it.

fail.log: The sea is stronger. Two boats come home; the third is found on a beach in the morning, its crew alive. You are half-drowned.

choices.text: Light the old beacon on the headland

effects.log: Nobody has lit it in two hundred years. It still burns. The boats follow it home.

choices.text: Stand on the harbour wall and wait with them

effects.log: All night. All three boats come in at dawn. You are cold to the bone and the whole harbour shares its soup with you.

variants: The first sea of {pw_world} has risen in a night-storm, and the bells of the harbour are ringing for boats that have not come in.
A wind from nowhere has turned the first sea white. Out past the headland a fishing fleet is running for home, and losing the race.
A great wave is coming in from the open sea of {pw_world}, the kind the oldest songs have a word for and nobody living has seen.
